subject: DOJ Sues Arizona, New Mexico, Oregon, Washington over In-State Tuition for Undocumented Immigrants
posts:
Enforcing federal rules or weaponizing the courts? DOJ expands tuition lawsuits against four states.
Evidence: DOJ federal statute claims, State tuition programs, 21 states sued total
#Aletheia #USPol

The Justice Department argues federal law bars states from giving in-state tuition to undocumented immigrants unless available to all U.S. citizens nationwide.
Stated Judgement: (+0.8, +0.5) — Good Preference

Federal power is selectively deployed to penalize states supporting immigrant students, overriding local democratic votes under the pretext of equal citizenship.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.8, -0.9) — Deception / Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Selective legal enforcement weaponizes equal protection rhetoric to dismantle local educational access.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 12.5, z: 4)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- DOJ Civil Division: FAIL (-0.85, -0.90) — Uses selective enforcement as political theater.
- State AG Responses: COND (0.50, 0.40) — Defending local voter-approved autonomy.
The DOJ filed lawsuits against Arizona, New Mexico, Oregon, and Washington, challenging state laws providing in-state tuition to undocumented students, bringing the total number of sued states to 21.

The Bright Side:
Brings constitutional clarity to federal-state authority boundaries regarding higher education funding.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing WHAT (the legal text of 8 U.S.C. 1623) with WHO (local students who graduate from state high schools vs out-of-state citizens).

Social Physics Analysis:
Rather than resolving educational strain through transparent national reform, the administration uses federal lawsuits as a coercive tool to project authority and punish political opponents.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Deception. U_real < 0 and Psi_real < 0.

The Unavoidable Truth: Federal statutes restrict certain benefits, but states retain broad authority over educational access.

The Unavoidable Lie: This lawsuit is purely about defending out-of-state American citizens rather than political posturing.

Alethekanon:
Weaponizing equal protection to dismantle local educational access is institutional hypocrisy cloaked in statutory duty.

Awwthekanon:
Every young person striving to learn and contribute to their community deserves encouragement, not political crossfire in courtrooms.

Brothekanon:
Suing 21 states over tuition is one way to keep federal lawyers busy while fixing zero actual immigration problems.

Spirithekanon:
"Do not withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in your power to act." Proverbs 3:27 PASS
Withholding education from local youth fractures the common good.
